intent.quote: When a user clearly answers to a specific question, that should be logged as an intent without having to have a new card created and re-asked the same question. The intent expression should be enough
intent.readback: plumb takes your intent only when you give it: when you open /plumb intent, answer an intent conflict, answer a question in the question tool or the study room, or reply to what the last message showed. It reads your words by what you mean, not by fixed wording, takes the part that is clear without asking it again, and asks only about what stays unclear. Each piece it takes is fitted into the intent already recorded, so the whole set stays coherent.
will: Keep each answer you give with the question, options and context it answered, so it is judged in context.
Close a question once you clearly answered it, and raise no new question about your answer.
Read your whole message with a language model independent of the coding agent, item by item: answered, change asked, reversed, or open.
Take the clear part of a mixed message and ask again, through the question tool, only the unclear part.
Fit every captured piece into the recorded intent; a change to older intent becomes one question for you to arbitrate.
When you say a judge-approved record misread you, re-formalize it and count the old version as a calibration 'no'; an intent change gets no label.
wont: Capture intent from an ordinary work request outside these moments.
Understand you with fixed word rules (affirmation or objection words, sentence splitting).
Ask you the same question again after a clear answer.
Let the agent's own relay or files stand for your words.
Ask you to approve, by id or by reading a card, what the AI wrote.
assumptions: P4's 'a card press' now means an answer given in the browser study room, since cards the owner presses are retired (P12).
Approval of the records an answer produces is the judge cascade's (P3, P9); this principle only captures and reads.
An ordinary request outside the loop goes through the edit gate of P6, not through capture.
No reachable reader model means plumb says so and holds (P8), never a fallback to word rules.
Both requirements sit under FEAT-008 (intent understood by models); the cluster anchors SR-130 and SR-163 carried no feature.

requirements.title: An owner answer is captured with the question it answered, once, and rationalized into the intent
requirements.statement: plumb captures intent only when the owner gives it: /plumb intent, an answer to an intent conflict, a question-tool or study-room answer, or a message answering what the last reply showed. Each piece is kept as a pre-intent with the question, options and context it answered, and the judge receives the question with the answer. A clear answer closes its question without raising another; an unclear or partial one leaves it open; a dismissed one captures nothing.

examples.given: the agent showed the 'where you answer a conflict' question in text with options 1, 2 and 3
examples.when: the owner replies '2'
examples.then: the question is answered with option 2, citing '2', and no new question about the reply '2' appears

examples.given: the agent's reply asked 'Merge now or after the review?'
examples.when: the owner replies 'after the review'
examples.then: the answer is captured with that question and no further question is raised for the reply

examples.given: a question with options 1, 2 and 3 shown in text
examples.when: the owner replies 'maybe 2, but I am not sure about the skills'
examples.then: the question stays open and nothing is captured as its answer

examples.given: a question about the reminder timing only
examples.when: the owner replies 'yes'
examples.then: only that question is answered; nothing the owner was not asked about is captured as their answer

examples.given: the agent asks 'Run the slow tests now or later?' with the question tool
examples.when: the owner picks 'later'
examples.then: plumb's log holds that question, both options and 'later' as the owner's answer in this session

examples.given: the owner's question-tool answer says 'yes, that is what I meant' about a requirement
examples.when: it is logged
examples.then: it is captured as a pre-intent with its question, and the requirement stays proposed until the judge cascade's verdict

examples.given: the owner dismisses the question without answering
examples.when: the tool returns
examples.then: nothing is logged as an answer

examples.given: an intent quoting "A" with the question offering A. Mostly in the background, B. A checkpoint every turn
examples.when: JEV judges the interpretation
examples.then: the claim it receives holds the question and the answer, not "A" alone

examples.given: a capture whose quote is "A" and no question
examples.when: the capture runs
examples.then: it warns that the answer needs its question and still records the intent

examples.given: a quote of a full sentence
examples.when: JEV judges it
examples.then: nothing is added to the quote

examples.given: a bare answer said to reply to a proposal plumb never showed
examples.when: the agent records it
examples.then: it is refused: the proposal it claims to answer was never shown

examples.given: no question is open and no intent loop is running
examples.when: the owner writes 'fix the typo in the README'
examples.then: no intent is captured from it; the request goes on as ordinary work

examples_dropped.why: it shows the answer on a card the owner reads; cards are retired (P12) and the question is kept with the answer by SR-097/EX-1
refusing a bare 'A' with no question contradicts confirmed SR-097/EX-2 (warn and still record), which holds
it makes a picked option wait for the owner's approval; under P3 and P9 the judge cascade decides and the owner is only asked questions

proof.plan: Recommended for the owner to decide: in a live session on a scratch repository, the agent asks one question through the question tool and the owner picks an option (the plumb line says the answer was kept with its question and no new question follows); the owner then answers a text question with 'maybe, not sure' (the question comes back once).

requirements.title: Each captured piece is rationalized into one coherent intent set
requirements.statement: Every captured piece is rationalized against the recorded intent so the set stays coherent on its own and between its elements: an answer that adds to an existing intent widens that intent rather than creating a second record, and one that changes or drops older intent is never recorded silently; it becomes one intent-conflict question to the owner through the question tool.

examples.given: recorded intent says reminders go by email
examples.when: the owner answers in the question tool 'also by SMS'
examples.then: the answer is rationalized into the set: the reminder intent now covers email and SMS, not two separate records

examples.given: recorded intent says reminders go by email only
examples.when: the owner answers 'send them by SMS instead'
examples.then: the change of older intent is not recorded silently: it becomes one intent-conflict question to the owner through the question tool

proof.plan: Recommended for the owner to decide: in a live session with a recorded reminder intent, the owner answers 'also by SMS' and the status shows one reminder intent covering both; then the owner answers 'by SMS instead' and gets one intent-conflict question.

requirements.title: The owner's message is read by meaning; the clear part is taken and only the unclear part asked again
requirements.statement: A reader model independent of the coding agent reads each hook-logged owner message by meaning, against the open questions and what the last reply showed, returning per item: answered, change asked, reversed or open, with its words and a confidence. An item counts as answered only when the last reply showed it at that version and the owner's words about it are in the message. The clear part at or above the calibrated threshold, which the owner's own answers set, is taken; only the rest is asked again through the question tool.

examples.given: a conflict question whose options are Keep this, Keep the other and Both
examples.when: the owner replies 'keep what main has'
examples.then: the reader names the option that side means and the conflict is settled on it

examples.given: a question with options 1, 2 and 3 shown in text
examples.when: the owner replies '2, and also make the pane resizable'
examples.then: the question is answered with option 2 and the pane request goes on as a new request, checked against confirmed intent; no question is raised for the '2'

examples.given: the same conflict question
examples.when: the owner replies 'hmm, either could work'
examples.then: the conflict stays open, nothing is recorded, and it is asked again through the question tool

examples.given: a message that answers a question and adds a request whose meaning the reader returns as open ('and do the thing with the pane')
examples.when: the reader runs
examples.then: the question is answered and only the pane request is asked about through the question tool, saying what was unclear

examples.given: the last reply showed the reminder intent and the plugin-UX requirement
examples.when: the owner writes 'the reminder part is fine, I am not sure about the UX one, some features might have to stay internal to plumb'
examples.then: the reminder item is answered as agreed with those words, and the UX requirement gets a change asked: some features stay internal to plumb

examples.given: the reader answers with a confidence of 0.7 and the threshold is 0.9
examples.when: plumb applies it
examples.then: nothing is taken and the item stays open

examples.given: the last reply showed only the reminder timing requirement
examples.when: the owner writes 'ok, and the export one is fine too'
examples.then: the reminder item is answered as agreed; the export requirement, not shown, is not taken as answered, and that part goes on as a new request checked against confirmed intent

examples.given: a question offering keep, drop or reword for an addition, and one offering two versions
examples.when: the owner answers 'keep it', 'drop it', 'reword to X', or 'the second, plus the first's date'
examples.then: the reader maps them to answered keep, answered drop, change (X) and change (the second version with the first's date)

examples.given: the last reply showed five items and left a question open
examples.when: the owner answers in one message
examples.then: one read job covers the message against all five items and the question, and returns one entry for each

examples.given: the owner has answered and the read job is still running
examples.when: the agent starts its next piece of work
examples.then: the progress shows plumb reading the answer, the agent proceeds, nothing is taken yet, and the answers are applied when the job returns

examples.given: twenty of the owner's answers show the owner agrees with the reader only above a confidence of 0.8
examples.when: the reader's threshold is recomputed
examples.then: the threshold becomes 0.8, the lowest confidence those answers support, instead of the starting 0.9

examples.given: the last reply showed the reminder timing requirement
examples.when: the owner writes 'Fine. Also add a dark mode to the settings page.'
examples.then: the reminder item is answered as agreed and the dark mode request goes on as a new request, not a reservation about the reminder

examples.given: the last reply showed the reminder timing requirement
examples.when: the owner writes 'Ok. The reminder should go out a day earlier.'
examples.then: the reader returns change asked (a day earlier) for the reminder, not agreement, since the second sentence is about it

examples.given: no reader model can be reached
examples.when: the owner's message needs reading
examples.then: plumb says so and holds the reading; nothing is taken by word rules

agent relay of an id-numbered answer list; relay and owner approval are gone (P2, P3)
agent relay; a reservation is now read by meaning (SR-187/EX-3 covers an unclear answer)
line-break parsing is a fixed word rule the reader replaces (INT-029)
owner confirms by id list; no ids, no approval (P2)
owner confirms decisions by id with 'ok'; no owner approval (P2, P3)
an ok held back on records; owner approval is gone, and a correction about a shown item is covered by SR-090/EX-8
an ok held back; covered by SR-090/EX-8 (a correction is a change asked)
an ok held back; covered by SR-090/EX-8 (a correction is a change asked)
plumb suggests to the agent what an ok confirms; there is no ok to relay
bare ok confirming cards; covered by SR-090/EX-2 without owner approval
carried by P3's relay-refused example under 'Only words plumb itself saw': an agent-run relay no longer exists
carried by P3's example 'a record edited after the question about it was put to the owner': the answer applies to the version asked about only and the edit goes back to the judge cascade

proof.plan: Recommended for the owner to decide: in a live session on a scratch repository, the last reply shows two items; the owner writes one message agreeing with one, changing the other and adding a new request (the plumb line shows each outcome and the new request goes on); an unclear sentence comes back as one question through the question tool. The reader's evaluation set runs as the command-level check.

requirements.title: A reversal re-formalizes the record, and counts as a calibration 'no' only when plumb misread the owner
requirements.statement: When the reader returns a judge-approved record as reversed by the owner's own logged words, the record is re-formalized and judged again. Its old version counts as a calibration 'no' only when the words say plumb misread them; a change of mind, or words that do not say, carries no label. Words no hook-logged prompt holds reverse nothing.

examples.given: a judge-approved intent and the owner's words 'that records your solution, not what I asked'
examples.when: the reader returns reversed, saying it misread the owner
examples.then: the old version counts as a calibration 'no', and the intent is re-formalized and judged again

examples.given: a judge-approved intent and the owner's words 'no, I don't know what to do with pi-agent-factory just yet'
examples.when: the reader returns reversed as an intent change
examples.then: the old version gets no calibration label and the intent is re-formalized

examples.given: a reversal whose words do not say whether the record misread them
examples.when: the reader returns it
examples.then: it is taken as an intent change, with no label, and the record is re-formalized

examples.given: words reversing a record that no prompt the hook logged holds
examples.when: the agent passes them on
examples.then: nothing is reversed

proof.plan: Recommended for the owner to decide: in a live session the owner says a judge-approved record misread them and sees it re-formalized, with the calibration count showing one more 'no'; then says they changed their mind about another and sees it re-formalized with no label.

decisions.question: How is a message taken that does only part of what the reader looks for?
decisions.chosen: Take what is clear: the clear part is applied, the unclear part stays open and is the only part asked again, through the question tool.
alternatives: Take nothing and ask the whole question again.

decisions.question: How should calibration treat a judge-approved record the owner reverses?
decisions.chosen: Re-formalize always; the old version counts as a calibration 'no' only when the owner says it misread their words; an intent change gets no label.
alternatives: Re-formalize always and never label the old version
Every reversal counts as a calibration 'no'

retired_decisions.why: it routes the 'Ask for a change' card button into the message box; cards and their buttons are retired (P12), and a change is said in conversation or in the question tool, read by meaning
